_comment: How each grading script emits a failure. The first version of the scanner hard-coded six
regexes modelled on enforcement-pack.ps1's idiom and applied them to all nine scripts, which
silently undercounted three of them — doc-lint.ps1 (missing its own headline rule, which
accumulates an object rather than a string), verify-kit.ps1 (7 of 16 Add-Finding FAIL sites
are single-quoted) and build-digests.ps1 (all 10 real rules use an $issues accumulator no
pattern named). Found by the phase 1 fresh-context review, F1.
Partial blindness is worse than total blindness: a script the scanner cannot see at all is
reported as NO EMISSION SITE FOUND, while one it half-sees reports a plausible number that
nobody questions. So the scanner now does two passes. 'accumulators' is the precise pass —
what this script actually uses. 'candidateSweep' in Coverage.Tests.ps1 is the recall pass — a
deliberately broad net whose hits, minus the precise ones, are printed as UNCLASSIFIED. That
difference is the measure of what the declaration might still be missing.
A script with an empty 'accumulators' list is DECLARED undeclared: its idiom has not been
worked out yet, it is reported as such, and the task that inventories it must resolve it.
Quote style is not part of these patterns — they stop before the message, so a single-quoted,
double-quoted, or non-literal message is a site either way.

scripts.note: Every member appends to one collection; the runner prints and exits 1. Warnings ($script:warnings) are deliberately not counted as failure sites — PhaseSizeWarning is a WARN rule and enters the inventory when phase 5 settles the vocabulary.
Prints and returns a per-commit verdict rather than accumulating.

UNDECLARED. Emits through a Write-Line wrapper that also carries informational and WARN lines, so naming the wrapper alone would inflate the denominator with non-rules. Resolve while inventorying it (tasks.md T029).
Three idioms, not one. $broken accumulates a PSCustomObject — the unresolved-path rule, which is doc-lint's headline check and was invisible to the first scanner.
A helper call, not an accumulator. Quote style varies across its 16 sites and one passes a variable.

The 10 distinct rules all land here. The Write-Host lines the first scanner found were the wrapper printing this collection — counting them measured the printer, not the rules. This is the script GAP-025 fixes in phase 2, so its baseline had to be right before that phase starts.
UNDECLARED. Reports CLEAN/OVERLAP and may emit no FAIL rule at all — which of the two is true is itself the question T034 must answer.
UNDECLARED. An aggregator: its only failure is 'a member failed'. Whether that is one rule or none is T035's question.
